tools.name: health
tools.description: Check whether the WEIR AI API is up. Use only when a call fails and you need to tell the user if WEIR AI is down. Returns {status, version, timestamp}. [Public, no account needed]

tools.name: discovery
tools.description: Read WEIR AI's public discovery document (public endpoints, base URL, rate limits). Use when you need to learn the API surface; for licensing questions use search_catalog instead. [Public, no account needed]

tools.name: license_types
tools.description: Explain WEIR AI's license types (open, earn, protect, blocked) in plain English. Use before explaining catalog results or when the user asks what a type allows. [Public, no account needed]

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search publicly discoverable WEIR AI identity licenses. Use when a user wants to find publicly listed likeness licensing options (e.g. for a campaign). Returns entries with license type, verification status and terms_url for reading the rights holder's published terms. Optional: search (text), licen

tools.name: check_identity
tools.description: Start here when anyone asks whether a real person's name, image or likeness can be used — in an ad, a campaign, generated media or a contract. Checks whether that person has publicly declared how their likeness may be used on WEIR AI. Required: name (full name, at least 3 characters). Returns status

tools.name: get_public_license
tools.description: Retrieve the public status, license category, available terms information, and terms link for a specific public WEIR license ID (e.g. WRT2TVR2A). Returns found:false with code NOT_FOUND_OR_NOT_PUBLIC when the ID is private or doesn't exist; that never reveals whether a private license exists and is

tools.name: search_mentions
tools.description: Search WEIR AI's supported web and social media sources for potential mentions associated with a person's name. The person does not need an existing WEIR identity or license. Results are candidate matches, not verified identification or evidence of infringement. Required: name (a person's full name;

tools.name: list_licenses
tools.description: List licenses the connected WEIR AI account owns or manages (including roster clients the account is permitted to see). Use for 'my licenses' or as the first step of monitoring. Optional page, per_page 1-100. Needs a connected WEIR AI account with license:read; if it returns AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED,

tools.name: get_license
tools.description: Get full detail of a license the connected account can access, by external_id. Use for the owner's own records; for the public catalog use get_public_license. Licenses the account can't access return NOT_FOUND_OR_NOT_PUBLIC. Needs license:read. [Needs a connected WEIR AI account; scope license:read]

tools.name: list_license_mentions
tools.description: Retrieve detected mentions for a license the connected user is authorized to monitor. Detection is not proof of infringement. Use the external_id already named in the conversation (e.g. from get_public_license); don't ask the user to repeat it. Returns rows with source link, date, type and status, r

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "check_identity" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: discovery, get_public_license · Private data: discovery, check_identity, get_public_license, get_license · Public sink: get_public_license.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: discovery, get_public_license · Private data: discovery, check_identity, get_public_license, get_license · Public sink: get_public_license

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
